key_insight: DFT screening shows K/Rb double perovskite halides β2SnGeX6 are stable, ductile, and highly tunable from wide-gap photovoltaic absorbers to low-gap thermoelectric materials.
engineering_relevance: The lead-free cubic compounds offer a promising materials platform for safer solar cells, tandem optoelectronics, and high-ZT waste-heat recovery devices.
method: Density functional theory (DFT) for structural, electronic, optical, and thermoelectric properties
Formation energy, tolerance factor, and octahedral factor analysis for stability screening
Elastic constants, band structures, and transport-related calculations for performance prediction
evidence_signal: The abstract reports thermodynamic stability for all six compositions, direct bandgaps tunable from 1.44 to 0.64 eV, and a peak thermoelectric figure of merit of ZT = 2.4 for K2SnGeI6 at 1000 K.
watch_item: Results are theoretical and depend on DFT approximations, so experimental synthesis, phase stability, and defect sensitivity still need validation.
paper_title: First-Principles Study of Novel Lead-Free Double Perovskite \b{eta}2SnGeX6 (\b{eta} = K, Rb; X = Cl, Br, I) for thermomechanical, optoelectronic and outstanding thermoelectric applications
